attacks.claim: Offline expiry relies on device time. A clock set back to a point between download and `valid_until` is not caught, and neither is a newer forecast issued while the phone is offline. The earlier-than-download guard and the issue time on the card cover the common cases, but the residual gap is untested.
attacks.evidence: "if the device clock reads earlier than that, the stored forecast is treated as expired."

attacks.claim: The rollback claim "no stale ratings remain on phones" is overstated. The flag and the purge only take effect when the app is foregrounded and can fetch config. The artifact also uses two different triggers: rollback says next foreground, QA says next launch. On-device expiry still limits the exposure window.
attacks.evidence: "takes effect on next app foreground ... so no stale ratings remain on phones" vs QA "purged on next launch"

attacks.claim: No CDN TTL or expiry-aware purge is stated for `/avy/v1/zones`, so the 10-minute freshness claim cannot be checked against the 92% hit rate. The client still enforces `valid_until`.
QA covers the screen-reader announcement only for live ratings. The expired and no-forecast states have no specified or tested announcement.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: VoiceOver/TalkBack text for "Forecast expired [time]" or "No current forecast"

attacks.claim: The agreement is cited for display only. Offline storage and CDN redistribution are not stated as permitted, and the max-of-three-bands zone color is not confirmed as a non-alteration. Legal confirmation would be prudent.
attacks.evidence: "display in our app is permitted"; "The zone color uses the highest of the three"

attacks.claim: The per-IP origin rate limit can hit users behind shared carrier or lodge IPs, and client handling of 429s is unspecified. The `bbox` size and alignment limits are also unstated, which could fragment the cache and add to origin cost. CDN spend has no estimate or cap.
attacks.evidence: "rate limited at origin to 120 req/min per IP"; "CDN budget alert at $400/month"
